question: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait it is observed that:

options.opa: The trait appears more frequently in males.
options.opb: The unaffected people do not transmit the trait.
options.opc: The trait tends to skip generations.
options.opd: The affected people have both affected parents.
options.ope: The trait tends to appear in the progeny of related parents.

reasoning_chain: CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears in both males and females equally" -> "trait does not appear more frequently in males" -> 20%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "unaffected individuals" -> "do not carry the trait allele" -> "do not transmit the trait" -> 95%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears in every generation" -> "trait does not skip generations" -> 10%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "affected individuals" -> "at least one affected parent" -> "not necessarily both parents affected" -> 30%
CHAIN: "Autosomal dominant trait" -> "trait appears in unrelated parents" -> "trait does not require related parents" -> 15%
analysis: In a pedigree of an autosomal dominant trait, the trait is typically passed from an affected parent to their offspring. Unaffected individuals do not carry the dominant allele and therefore do not transmit the trait to their children. This is a key characteristic of autosomal dominant inheritance patterns.
